paper_title: Thinking Slow, Fast Scaling Inference Compute with Distilled Reasoners
caption: : Coverage.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the coverage performance of four different models—Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT—as a function of the number of completions (k), where k ranges from 2⁰ to 2⁸ on a logarithmic x-axis. The y-axis, labeled “Coverage,” spans from 0.2 to 1.0 in linear scale, with major tick marks at intervals of 0.2. All four lines show a generally increasing trend in coverage as k increases. The Llama-3B model (solid blue line with circular markers) starts at approximately 0.43 at k=1 and rises to about 0.91 at k=256. The Llama-3B + FT model (dashed green line with triangular markers) begins slightly lower at ~0.42 and reaches ~0.90 at k=256, closely tracking Llama-3B. The Llama-1B model (solid light blue line with square markers) starts at ~0.28 and climbs to ~0.85. The Llama-1B + FT model (dashed light green line with diamond markers) begins at ~0.27 and ends at ~0.83, consistently trailing its non-finetuned counterpart. All curves exhibit diminishing returns as k increases, with the steepest gains occurring between k=1 and k=16.
